blockers: the security mode must be shown to be unrecoverable from the network features alone (firewall_lab.mode_leakage). UPDATED 2026-09-01: this blocker previously said it was waiting for paired sessions from the formal campaign. Those sessions arrived on 2026-08-13/14 (1,100 paired sessions, 550 per mode) and the measurement was made: cross-mode separability is 0.9451 against a 0.70 threshold. The question this blocker asked has therefore been answered, and the answer is negative -- the security mode IS recoverable from the network features, because DDS Security changes the shape of the traffic. That measurement is what forced per-mode training, and it is a methodological finding rather than a defect. The blocker stands, but its reason has changed from 'not yet measured' to 'measured and unmet'. Whether the requirement still applies at all once each model only ever sees one mode is a design decision that has not been made; it must not be assumed by this file.

two lab defects of exactly this kind have already been found by hand -- Permissive on shared memory while Enforce was forced onto UDP, and an Enforce-only source address -- so an RQ3 claim must not rest on the absence of a third being assumed
